title: 18 of 71 open `domain:spec` `pm:queue` cards say in their own body that their disposition is a maintainer decision — they read as dispatchable and are not
body:
⛔ **Filed unlabelled and ungraded** by the `domain:spec` execution seat, session `session_01MkQhmuuJAVDjmeWNixwDDH`, 2026-09-12T10:02Z. `domain:*`, type and priority are triage's. ⛔ Not claimed, ⛔ not dispatched, and ⛔ this seat answers none of the questions the cards below raise.

## The pattern, and why it costs something

A card sitting in `pm:queue` reads as **dispatchable**. A card whose disposition is a maintainer-floor decision is not. When both look identical on the board, every dispatcher that reaches one of the second kind does one of two things:

- **skips it silently** — leaving no record, so the next dispatcher rediscovers it from scratch; or
- **dispatches it** — and the round hits the fence on its first measurement and stops, which is the expensive outcome.

Both happened in this lane today. Three cards were handed back individually with `pm:retriage` (#17598, #16066, #17534) after being read one at a time during card selection. ⭐ That is the reactive form of this card: it fixes one card per encounter and never reaches the rest.

## Measured, 2026-09-12T10:0xZ

Over **every** open `domain:spec` + `pm:queue` card — 71 of them, enumerated by label rather than sampled:

> **18** carry, **in their own body**, a sentence naming a maintainer-floor or decision disposition, and **none of the 18 carries `pm:retriage`.**

```
14512  15124  15932  16075  16160  16282  16348  16524  16870
16906  17108  17109  17158  17296  17319  17321  17518  17594
```

The probe is a phrase match over the card bodies: `maintainer ruling` · `is a contract decision` · `not a door fix` · `ruling-grade` · `maintainer decision` · `narrows a published accept set` · `人工地板` · `is a decision` · `not_planned`, case-insensitive, `pm:retriage` carriers excluded.

## ⛔ 18 is an UPPER BOUND, and here is a verified false positive

⭐ **A string count is not a reading of meaning**, and this probe demonstrates it. **#17594** is in the list because it contains `ruling-grade` — but the sentence it appears in is the card **excluding** that question from itself:

> ⛔ No claim the conversions should delete the node. That is a **ruling-grade** question … This card is about the **todo**, ⛔ not the conversion's behaviour.

⇒ #17594 is mechanical and dispatchable; this seat has already read it, confirmed that, and is holding it only for file contention on `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`. **At least one of the 18 is a false positive because the phrase appears in a sentence that fences the floor OUT.** Others may be. ⇒ the list is a **worklist to read**, ⛔ not a verdict on 18 cards, and ⛔ nothing here should be re-graded from the probe alone.

Two of the 18 are already known to this seat by reading rather than by probe: **#16282** (the real repair is a published accept-set change) and **#15932** (its own text: "retiring a `packages/spec` surface is a maintainer ruling plus the `spec-property-retirement` playbook").

## The ask

⛔ Not a re-grading request on any specific card, and ⛔ not an opinion on any disposition. The ask is that triage decide **whether this population wants a sweep** — read each of the 18, and for the ones that really are floor-shaped, move them out of the dispatch queue (decision box with the four-facet block and 維護者速讀, or `not_planned`, or a split where only part is floor-shaped, as #17598 needs).

⚠️ If the answer is "no sweep, keep handing them back one at a time", that is a legitimate answer and this card closes `not_planned` — the value was in measuring the population, which had never been counted.

## What this card does NOT claim

- ⛔ No claim that any of the 18 is wrongly graded — the probe cannot support that and the false positive proves it.
- ⛔ No claim about cards outside `domain:spec` + `pm:queue`; the enumeration is bounded to that label pair and to open cards, read at 2026-09-12T10:0xZ.
- ⛔ No claim that the decision box is the right destination for any particular card; split and `not_planned` are live options per card.
- ⛔ No severity, no priority, no `domain:*`.
